steps: Separate isolated-test approval; fresh identity, collision check and exact two-resource change-set inspection. No Legacy resources, roles or authority changes.
Provision only the owned isolated bucket/SSL policy. Record bucket identity and empty contents. No public access, versioning, lifecycle or CMK.
Sign exactly one PUT for the fixed synthetic key/body. Keep Authorization/URL in memory only. Send the first body chunk, hold remaining chunks, record request-start timing without credentials.

Install the exact all-principal logo fence on the isolated bucket while PUT is open; read back its complete hash. Send a fresh guarded request to demonstrate effective denial independently of the open PUT.

Resume the original body stream and capture terminal status/request ID; HEAD/list the exact key, size and digest metadata. Record whether an already-started request committed after denial became effective.

Repeat only if separately approved and the prior request is terminal; no automatic retry after ambiguous failure. Distinguish direct SigV4 and presigned PUT; a presigned download example is not upload proof.

Restore only the isolated initial SSL policy, then remove only the matching synthetic object after content/identity checks. Verify no unexpected objects, remove the two temporary resources and confirm absence.

bounds.streaming: Controlled local runner with explicit pause/resume; abort connection on deadline, then verify terminal AWS/object outcome rather than assuming cancellation

interpretation.lateCommit: Confirms fence/expiry cannot substitute for draining accepted requests. Require a separately reviewed source-writer/upload quiescence mechanism before maintenance.
interpretation.denied: One isolated result does not establish a universal maximum lifetime or enumerate real in-flight PUTs. Review source request lifecycle and operator/issuance evidence before choosing a bound.
interpretation.unknown: Gate remains blocked; preserve partial evidence and perform safe isolated cleanup only.

actualSourceRequirement: Do not enter real FROZEN until a supported source quiescence procedure is reviewed; do not transfer TARGET without terminal/correlation evidence that admitted Legacy data-plane operations cannot commit later. ListMultipartUploads covers multipart metadata only, not in-flight single-part PUTs.
remainingDecision: A 300-second presigned expiry, 900-second cleanup-provider timeout and repeated empty listings are supporting observations, not by themselves a certificate that all admitted S3 uploads ended.
